subject: Agriculture
title: Pheromone Traps
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pheromone Traps usable.

hook.text: Male moths follow female scent for miles. Synthetic pheromones exploit this drive to lure them into traps.

buildup.text: Pheromones are species-specific chemicals insects use to find mates. Scientists synthesize them in labs.

discovery.text: Traps baited with pheromones catch specific pest species without harming any other organisms. Zero collateral damage.

twist.text: Mating disruption floods orchards with pheromone so males can't find real females. Populations crash without a single kill.

climax.text: Pheromone-based control now protects most US apple orchards from codling moth—the industry's worst pest.

punchline.text: Confuse the males, crash the population. The gentlest pest control ever.

quiz.question: How does mating disruption with pheromones work?
options: Flooding the area with pheromone prevents males from finding real females

details.summary: Pheromone traps use synthetic versions of insect sex pheromones to attract and capture or confuse pest insects. This topic covers how pheromone-based strategies work for monitoring and mating disruption, their use in IPM programs, and their advantages over chemical sprays.
details.whyItMatters: Pheromone technology provides species-specific pest control without toxic residues. Mating disruption using pheromones has dramatically reduced insecticide use in orchards and vineyards while maintaining effective pest control.
takeaways: Pheromone traps attract specific pest species using synthetic versions of sex pheromones
They are used for monitoring pest populations and timing spray applications precisely
Mating disruption floods fields with pheromone to prevent males from finding females

faq.question: How do pheromone traps differ from conventional insect traps?
faq.answer: Pheromone traps use synthetic sex pheromones that attract only the target pest species, while light traps and sticky traps catch many non-target insects. This specificity means pheromone traps can monitor specific pest populations precisely without harming beneficial insects.

faq.question: What is mating disruption and how effective is it?
faq.answer: Mating disruption deploys thousands of pheromone dispensers per hectare, flooding the air with synthetic pheromone so males cannot locate females. It has reduced codling moth damage in apple orchards by 90-99% and cut insecticide applications by 70-80% in many fruit and vine crops.
